I can’t browse the web from here, and I’m not allowed to assert current time‑sensitive release status from memory. I can, however, give concise, authoritative ways to check now and a couple quick commands you can run.

What to check (authoritative sources)
- Official PostgreSQL site (downloads / front page): https://www.postgresql.org/
- Official announcement/news archive: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/
- Official source tarball listing (shows released versions): https://ftp.postgresql.org/pub/source/

Quick commands you can run from this machine (no browser needed)
- Find the newest source tarball name:
  curl -s https://ftp.postgresql.org/pub/source/ | grep -o 'postgresql-[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+' | sort -V | tail -1
- Extract the major version from that:
  curl -s https://ftp.postgresql.org/pub/source/ | grep -o 'postgresql-[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+' | sort -V | tail -1 | sed 's/postgresql-\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/'
- If you have psql locally, check its version:
  psql --version
  or, in SQL:
  SELECT version();

If you paste the output of the first curl command here, I’ll tell you exactly which major is current and whether PostgreSQL 18 appears in the released list.
